assumptions: Agencies have enough recurring certificate orders and coordination burden to prefer one accountable service.
Licensed assessors can be recruited nonexclusively at payouts that preserve the stated contribution margin.
The platform can avoid taking professional responsibility for certificate accuracy while still guaranteeing service quality.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Two paid agency pilots showing monthly order density, assessor fill rates, turnaround improvement, support minutes, repeat ordering, CAC, and at least 35% contribution margin, plus renewable workflow agreements and a dependable assessor panel.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Embedding licensed-assessor capacity at a legally triggered property event is a sensible workflow thesis, but it is primarily an aggregation and convenience play rather than a structurally novel mechanism.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Every qualifying transaction creates an established paid service event, so willingness to pay for the certificate is strong; willingness to pay an additional platform margin for routing and SLA remains unvalidated.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Prepaid orders and agency aggregation aid cash conversion, but 25-40% contribution margins, human coordination, low-cost assessor competition, infrequent property-level repeat, and ambitious order-volume assumptions weaken operating leverage.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Estate agencies and property managers provide a clear recurring-order beachhead, although the Polish market's achievable order density and platform net revenue are not evidenced.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Assessor marketplaces, direct local assessors, and agency-owned panels are easy alternatives. Domination would require workflow placement and unusually reliable capacity rather than the API alone.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: The ordering relationship could extend into inspections, renovation documentation, property compliance, financing, and additional professional services.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Reliability data, integrations, and agency habits can build modest switching costs, but assessor supply is nonexclusive and competitors can copy routing and status features.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Fast, dependable fulfillment and document completeness could improve convenience and closing certainty, but no SLA, delay reduction, or economic advantage has been demonstrated.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The legal certificate trigger supports continuing demand now, but ten-year validity and the absence of a new acute transition limit exceptional momentum.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Two-agency manual service is a credible validation route and agency integrations can aggregate demand, but no channel access or referral agreement exists and account acquisition still requires relationship selling.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: Manual dispatch can launch within available capital and time, with assessors retaining professional issuance, though quality control, complaints, supply coverage, and thin margins remain material.

highest_value_structural_change: Own the pre-closing workflow through an exclusive or deeply embedded agency/property-management integration with contracted regional SLA capacity, rather than competing as a general certificate marketplace.
main_structural_strength: Demand is tied to a current legal transaction and can be validated cheaply through manual fulfillment before building integrations.
primary_score_limiter: Thin intermediation margins and nonexclusive supply provide limited defense against direct assessors, marketplaces, or agency-owned panels.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Certificates generally remain valid for ten years and low-cost direct assessors can compress both repeat frequency and platform take rates.
